facts.statement: The genus was named after Øystein Djupedal, a former Norwegian minister who funded the excavation with 1.2 million kroner.
facts.quote: It is named after Øystein Djupedal, the former Minister of Education and Research who helped fund the fossil excavation with a budget of 1.2 million Norwegian kroner.

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in 2009 in Spitsbergen within the Agardhfjellet Formation.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles aparecieron en 2009 en Spitsbergen, en la Formación Agardhfjellet

facts.statement: The fossils are dated to the middle Volgian stage.
facts.quote: y se ha datado en el Volgiano medio.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, PMO 216.839, is a partially preserved juvenile plesiosaur.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo (PMO 216.839) pertenece a un plesiosaurio juvenil conservado parcialmente.

facts.statement: The animal lived in the uppermost Jurassic in central Spitsbergen, Norway.
facts.quote: Djupedalia is an extinct genus of cryptoclidid plesiosauroid plesiosaur known from the uppermost Jurassic of central Spitsbergen, Norway.

facts.statement: Djupedalia belongs to the family Cryptoclididae.
The genus lived between 149.2 and 143.1 million years ago during the Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 143.1 million years ago)
